title: SLO-priority-radar-and-launch-readiness-runbook (working)
content:
Purpose / context:
This working sheet defines a compact, SLO-weighted prioritization radar for pre-launch readiness and a minimal launch runbook checklist. Goal is to give PMs and ops a fast decision surface for triage during the 2-week launch window. Not a canonical product-ops playbook (that lives in Confluence), this is a working prioritizer that feeds into on-call decisions and go/no-go signaling.

Quick summary of approach:
- Each launch signal (availability, latency, cost, quality, security) is normalized to a 0-100 score.
- Apply business weight to signals to get a single Launch Risk Score (LRS).
- LRS drives triage bucket: Red (>=70), Amber (40-69), Green (<40).
- For Red signals, owners must declare an action within 30 minutes during launch operations.

Scoring model (simple / auditable):
- availability_score = (1 - p50_error_rate) * 100  // p50_error_rate expressed as fraction of requests failing
- latency_index = clamp( (observed_p95_ms / target_p95_ms) * 100, 0, 200 )
- cost_delta = clamp( (current_cost / baseline_cost) * 100, 50, 300 )  // caps to avoid outliers
- quality_score = (1 - quality_regression_rate) * 100  // e.g., eval set regressions
- security_score = 100 if no incidents, 30 if non-critical finding, 0 if active incident

LRS formula (example weights, adjustable per launch):
LRS = round( 0.35*(100 - availability_score) + 0.30*(latency_index - 100) + 0.15*(100 - quality_score) + 0.10*(cost_delta - 100) + 0.10*(100 - security_score) )
Notes: higher LRS == more risk. LRS range approx -? to 200 depending on caps; we clamp to 0-100 for UI.

Priority radar (how to interpret buckets):
- RED (70-100): immediate mitigation required. Consider rollback to previous model version, throttling, traffic hold, or route to dedicated capacity.
- AMBER (40-69): monitor closely with rapid mitigations (cache priming, reduce batch sizes, apply KV cache bypass). Prepare owners for escalation.
- GREEN (0-39): proceed. Continue metric sampling and smoke checks.

Example run of 2025-03-01 smoke test (mock numbers):
- observed p50_error_rate: 0.004 -> availability_score = 99.6
- observed_p95_ms: 420ms, target_p95_ms: 300ms -> latency_index = 140 -> contribution = 0.30*(140-100)=12
- current_cost vs baseline: 1.12 -> cost_delta = 112 -> contribution = 0.10*(112-100)=1.2
- quality_regression_rate: 0.015 -> quality_score=98.5 -> contribution = 0.15*(100-98.5)=0.225
- security: no incidents -> security_score=100 -> contribution=0
LRS rough = 0.35*(0.4) + 12 + 0.225 + 1.2 = ~13.8 -> clamp -> AMBER (because latency is main driver).

Minimum launch readiness checklist (owners + expected signal):
- Traffic gating plan defined and tested (owner: Samir Das) [expected: traffic can be shifted to dedicated within 10 minutes]
- Model fallback matrix documented (owner: Lena Ortiz) [expected: compatible variant available and validated]
- Observability slices: token-level cost, p95 latency per model, error-rate by route (owner: Omar Al-Khalili) [expected: dashboard + alert thresholds set]
- Canary traffic schedule + automatic rollback criteria (owner: Maya Chen) [expected: canary < 0.5% for first 30m; rollback if LRS>=70 for 5m]
- Eval prompt set sanity checks (owner: Ravi Patel) [expected: no quality regressions >1.5% on core prompt set]
- Security posture sweep completed (owner: Security Eng rep) [expected: no high/critical unresolved findings]
- On-call rota and escalation contact list up-to-date (owner: Product-ops lead)

Triage play cards (quick actions by bucket):
- RED:
  * Immediately reduce traffic to affected model (via routing policy)
  * Switch to verified fallback or previous model version
  * If latency spike only: move heavy requests to dedicated pool or enable smaller batch sizes and bypass KV cache for new sessions
  * Notify execs + customer-success for affected customers
- AMBER:
  * Enable cache priming and re-run hot prompts on standby hardware
  * Deploy a config tweak (e.g., reduce max_tokens, disable non-essential post-processing) with canary
  * Increase sampling of eval telemetry and compare against golden prompts
- GREEN:
  * Continue normal monitoring and log intervals for post-launch retrospective

Compact KPI table (suggested columns for the sheet view):
- KPI name | owner | current value | baseline | target | weight | normalized score | notes/action
Example rows (plain text):
- p95 latency | Omar Al-Khalili | 420ms | 300ms | <=350ms | 0.30 | 140 | heavy inference on long-sequence prompts
- error rate (p50) | Samir Das | 0.4% | 0.2% | <=0.5% | 0.35 | 99.6 | transient DB timeouts in staging
- eval quality reg | Ravi Patel | 1.5% | 0.5% | <=1.0% | 0.15 | 98.5 | slight hallucination uptick for finance prompts
- cost per 1k tokens | Finance | $14.2 | $12.7 | <=$13.5 | 0.10 | 112 | spike during batch reprofiling
- security finding | Security | none | none | none | 0.10 | 100 | last sweep OK

Open questions / unresolved ideas (notes-to-self):
- Should we make latency_index asymmetric (punish overshoot more than undershoot)? front-load for user-facing endpoints.
- How to incorporate business-critical customer weights into LRS (per-customer multiplier)? propose per-launch override field.
- Automate LRS in ops runbook with a 30s cadence and a sliding 5-minute median to avoid flapping.

Immediate next steps (this doc):
- Convert this sheet into a live Google Sheet with the KPI columns above and a small script that computes LRS (owner: Maya Chen) - target: 2025-03-06
- Add runbook snippets to Confluence with decision tree and links to rollback playbooks (owner: Samir) - target: 2025-03-08
- Run two dry-run drills with the SRE and serving-runtime teams to validate switch times (owner: Lena) - dates: 2025-03-10, 2025-03-12

Log / edit history (brief):
- 2025-02-14 initial sketch
- 2025-02-28 weight tuning and scoring formula added
- 2025-03-01 mock smoke data added
- 2025-03-04 updated owner list and next steps

If you are reading this during an active launch: copy the KPI table to the ops channel, set alerts to page owners when any single KPI crosses its threshold, and follow the triage play cards above.

End of working sheet.
